title: The Minor Scale Recipe
description: A different mix of whole and half steps, and a much moodier scale.

steps.title: A different pattern
steps.description:
The natural minor scale has its own pattern of whole steps (W) and half steps (H):

W - H - W - W - H - W - W

Compare it with a major scale from the same note and three notes come out one key lower: the 3rd, the 6th and the 7th. Those three lowered notes are where the darker mood comes from.

steps.title: A natural minor
steps.description: Play the white keys from A up to G. They're the same keys as C major, but starting on A makes the whole thing sound sadder.
steps.hint: All white keys from A to G.

steps.title: Walking it from A
steps.description:
Here's the pattern traced from A:

• A, whole step to B
• B, half step to C (white keys touching)
• C, whole step to D
• D, whole step to E
• E, half step to F (white keys touching)
• F, whole step to G
• G, whole step back to A

The half steps fall right where the keyboard already has them, so A minor needs no black keys.

steps.title: D natural minor
steps.description: Start the pattern on D: D, E, F, G, A, and then a half step up from A. That means Bb, not B.
steps.hint: D, E, F, G, A, Bb, C. One black key, just left of B.

steps.title: E natural minor
steps.description: From E, the first step is a whole step, so you jump right over F to F#. Everything after that is white keys.
steps.hint: E, F#, G, A, B, C, D.
